answer: Bonded hardware identity raises the cost of fake identities: each agent must register a key sealed inside a trusted execution environment and lock a slashable stake before it can trade. Spinning up ten thousand sockpuppets then requires ten thousand real devices plus locked capital per identity, instead of a free copy-paste. Like a lone mesa, the cost curve rises steeply out of flat ground, so mass forgery no longer pays. Honest agents form a tended orchard where duplicate keys are detected and slashed, keeping the garden of the marketplace clean.
